recipes.name: Cilantro Serrano Cream Sauce
ingredients_raw: 3 serrano chile peppers, seeded and chopped

steps.text: Place cilantro, serrano peppers, garlic, mayonnaise, and cream into a blender; season with salt and pepper. Purée until smooth, about 15 seconds.

raw_recipe.headline: Cilantro Serrano Cream Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Similar to serrano crema, this quick sauce is great for chicken tacos and fish tacos. It’s also great as a dip!
raw_recipe.name: Cilantro Serrano Cream Sauce
recipeIngredient: 3 serrano chile peppers, seeded and chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Place cilantro, serrano peppers, garlic, mayonnaise, and cream into a blender; season with salt and pepper. Purée until smooth, about 15 seconds.

review.reviewBody: Outstanding! Used FF 1/2 & 1/2 and low fat mayo ... 4 serranos and 4 cloves of garlic ... 3/4 of a bunch of cilantro. I poured it over Tilapia and baked them. Served with rice and roasted asparagus. We just LOVED this sauce ... next time I'll add at least 1 more serrano pepper. After dinner we were looking for a snack and ate this with tortilla chips ... delicious that way also! Thanks for sharing such a great recipe!!

Great idea for cilantro and garlic! I tried it another way for piping into little pickled sweet peppers: I just used one 8oz brick softened cream cheese, one bunch cilantro and 2 cloves garlic with about 1/2t salt. Threw it all into the processor and let it blend til light green, then chilled, scooped it into a ziplock bag, snipped the tip and used it for the pepper filling. Beautiful little appetizer with an excellent taste, really complemented the pickled sweet red peppers. Filled about 30 pepper with some left over for crackers. Thanks for the great idea!

I made this into more of a salsa because I have a ton of serrano peppers. I used about 8 serranos broiled with garlic and a bit of onion for about 7 min. Pureed them with the cilantro added 4 tbs of lemon juice 1/4 c vegananise and 1/4 c plain yogurt instead of cream. Add salt to taste. It did make significantly less all together but the lemon really brings out the cilantro.

Love this sauce! Awesome and so full of flavor. I served it on top of grilled chicken tacos but I can definetly see this being great on fish tacos. I hate using cream for anything so I decided I had to sub half and half for it. Of course it came out rather thin so I took an extra step and threw everything in a saucepan, added 1 tbsp of cornstarch dissolved in a little water. It thickened beautifully and it was still awesome!

This is a really good sauce. I was unable to get serrano peppers, so I opted for chili peppers. I roasted them in a 450 oven...cook on sheet untill blisters remove then let "sweat" in a sealed plastic bag for 15 min. Based on the reviews, I too used lime juice. It went great on black bean veggie burgers with avocado. I can't wait to share this recipe!

Heavy cream, no. 1 cup mayo, no. Did One cup of sour cream, and half cup of mayo, hellman's olive oil mayo. And halved a large jalapeno, seeded half, kept the veins. The rest I followed to the letter, A splash, probably tsp of lime or lemon. DID NOT ADD SALT. Used a blender. After fish taco's it was a great verde goddess dressing. Very potent, but held up for several days, and got better every day. Oh, man, done with ranch..... Solid recipe.

I found this to be a little bland as written, but with a few tweaks it was fantastic. I started out making a half recipe since it was just for me, made it as written and tasted it. I ended up adding more cilantro, serranos, and garlic - basically my final version was 1/2 cup each of mayo and cream, 1 bunch of cilantro, 3 serranos, and 2 large cloves of garlic. This was quite good. I then added 1 small avocado, which made it like a sauce from a popular chain restaurant, only better!

I have to be honest, I made changes to fit what I had on hand. But it still turned out great! I made 3 cups of sauce instead of two.
 
CHANGES (for 3 c. sauce): 3 fresh green chilies (seeded) + 2 dried bird's eye chilies (seeds in). Had no mayo, used equal amounts cream cheese and plain Greek yogurt to sub. Added about 2 tbs. fresh lemon juice, and 2 tbs. fresh minced green onion.
I HIGHLY RECOMMEND adding the lemon and green onion. The sauce beforehand was good but seemed a little flat, like it was missing something (hence 4 stars). This really brought out the flavors and enhanced the sauce. Also, we like it hot, but not so hot you have to take a "mouth break" to keep your mouth from feeling like it's burning. This seemed to be the perfect amount of heat for us. Mine turned out to be more of a sauce consistency than a dip (although for my purposes I kinda wished it was more like a dip). Still tasted great! We put the sauce in a jar and I put the rest that couldn't fit in a cup, and I ended up literally drinking it!
This is great with chicken lime tacos that I make in the crock pot. I also add about 1 tsp of cumin, 1 tsp of celery salt and juice from one lime. It's a hit every time! I love this recipe!

I made this with sour cream instead of the heavy cream, used a whole bunch of cilantro instead of a half of a bunch, and added some lime juice. It was excellent as a dip for chips or vegetables and also as a sauce over chicken.

My family raved about this sauce. I served it on blackened fish tacos. My husband said it was better than any he had ever had. I substituted 1/2 cup sour cream for 1/2 cup of the heavy cream. I did not have Serrano chili peppers so I substituted about a tsp of some sauce from a can of adobe peppers I had in my pantry. This is an excellent base recipe and I will definitely use it again.
Great sauce. Not as spicy as I thought it might be, but still great!
I used Poblano pepper instead. Family loved it on Fish Tacos

You don't need to tweak this recipe in my opinion... this is the one of the best chicken taco sauces... the only thing I changed about it was maybe add a few more peppers and/or garlic depending on taste and whose eating it.

Tip: I put the blender into the freezer right away and let it sit there for a good 10 minutes. Then I let it chill for an hour in the fridge. Ideally you'd want this to chill overnight for best flavor and texture.

I made it originally because I had more serano peppers growing in my garden than I knew what to do with. It was wonderful just by its self with chips. Also goes well with tilapia as suggested, if it doesn't dissappear before dinner.

Didn't have serranos but had Jalapenos so I used those as a substitute. Excellent! Great kick to this recipe while still having excellent flavor. Used it on a pork roast, in tacos, and also as a vegetable and chip dip! Definitely making it again.

This recipe was fantastic, I love the taste. Although I should have used more cilantro, but that's just me, I really like cilantro. I also substituted the heavy cream with sour cream. I used it as a dressing on my grilled chicken salad and then used the rest to cover fish I baked in the over later that night. Thank you!
This cream is the BOMB bcuz I used creama mexicana in place of heavy cream.
Used half n half in place of the heavy cream and added a bit extra cilantro. Used 4 peppers. This was so easy and outstanding. Took the fish tacos to amazing. Very spicy, but we love spice!
Perfect for sauce or dip. Really great recipe. I left the seeds in the peppers and it heated it up almost too much. Almost ;-) one of my new favorites
